beats.say: Good morning. And welcome to Passionfruit Park.
It's a beautiful day here at our campus. The sun is rising. The birds are singing. Several of the birds are under contract.
Every year, we gather to share the things we've been working on. And every year, we say this is our biggest year ever.
Ten years ago, we made our first product. It was a juicer. It was too thin to juice anything. And we realized, that's not a juicer. That's a philosophy.
This year is no different. This year is our biggest year ever. It is also our thinnest year ever. And you'll see what we mean.
We have new phones. New wearables. New ways to hear less. And something we have been calling, internally, the thing.
So let's get started. Let's walk.
At Passionfruit, we believe technology should be simple. So simple that it disappears.
Over the years, we removed the headphone jack. Then the charger. Then the box. Then the buttons.
This year, our engineers asked a bold question. What else can we remove?
The answer, it turns out, was almost everything. And we did it. We removed almost everything.
We kept the price.
To tell you more, let's head inside. Our design team has been waiting for us since six this morning. They are very excited. They are also very cold.
You may notice we're recording this in an empty theater. That was a design decision.
We wanted the room to feel the way our products feel. Quiet. Spacious. Mostly air.
We start, as always, with the device you use most. The device you look at two hundred times a day. Three hundred, if the meeting is long.
And to tell you how we made it, here's the person who made us make it. Imogen.
When we began work on the new phone, we didn't begin with a phone. We began with a feeling.
The feeling of holding something precious. Something light. Something you might lose at any moment.
We studied the corner for nearly three years. We asked, what is a corner, really? What does it want?
And we discovered that a corner wants to be round. Just a little. Just enough to forgive you.
Every surface was considered. Then reconsidered. Then considered again by a different team, who disagreed with the first team, beautifully.
The result is a phone carved from a single block of titanium. And then, mostly, carved away.
Hold it, and you'll notice it isn't there. That's the point. It's there. You just don't notice.
This is the most Passionfruit phone we've ever made. We are so proud to introduce it.
Introducing Pulp Phone One.
Aerospace-grade titanium. Polished, then polished again, then asked to reflect on itself.
Seven cameras. Arranged in a way that is, frankly, a lot.
Inside, an all-new design. We moved the battery, the logic board and the glass closer together, until they had nowhere left to go.
At its edges, Pulp Phone One is zero point zero millimeters thick. Technically, it only has one side.

beats.text: So thin it has only one side.
beats.sub: The other side is coming next year.

beats.say: Available in five colors. Passion Purple. Golden Pulp. Pith. Seed. And a bold new Rind.
I'd like to say a word about color. Because color is not decoration. Color is a promise.
Our new shade, Rind, took two years. We started with orange. Then we asked, what if it were more orange. Then we asked, what if it were orange, but sad.
There was a period where it was briefly beige. We don't talk about that. Some of the team still can't.
And then, one morning, the sun came through that window, and hit a passionfruit someone had left on the desk. And we knew. Rind.
It's the color of a sunrise you see on purpose. We hope you'll see it every day. Ideally on a phone you can find.
Hi. Hello. I'm Theo. I lead the thinness team. It's a small team. It used to be bigger. We made it thinner.
Making a phone this thin raised a lot of questions. Mostly from me. At night.
So we built this lab to test it. These robots have dropped Pulp Phone One forty thousand times.
We found it again thirty-one thousand times. Which, statistically, is great.
We also bend tested it. With a hydraulic press. With a person sitting on it. With a person sitting on the hydraulic press.
It passed every test. Well, it passed through every test. Like, physically. Through the test. The test equipment is fine. Mostly.
One thing we learned is that the phone is so thin that you can't really find it. Which is why every Pulp Phone One ships with a second phone. To find it.
The second phone is also very thin. We're working on it. Okay. Back to you, Dana. Is that it? Am I done? I'm done.
Of course, a phone this thin needs a chip this smart. So we designed our own. Again. From scratch. Again.
It's called P1 Pith. It has forty billion transistors. We named all of them. It took a while.
P1 Pith is up to forty percent faster than the chip it replaces, which was also ours, and which we were very excited about last year. We've moved on.
And it delivers all-day battery life. All day, of course, being defined as the day of this event. After that, it's really up to you.
P1 Pith.
A sixteen-core neural engine, trained exclusively on photos of fruit.
An all-new performance core. An all-new efficiency core. And an all-new core that just watches the other cores work, and nods.

beats.sub: Every core. Even the nodding one.

beats.say: The all-new camera system. Seven lenses. Including our first ever lens that points at the other lenses.
Take photos in the dark. Take photos of the dark. Take photos of other people taking photos, in the dark.
And for those who want more, there's Pulp Phone One Max. Our largest phone ever. Also our thinnest ever. We don't know how either.
With a display so big, it's technically a tablet. Our tablet team has been informed. They are taking it well.
Theo! You made it up here. Great. Let's show everybody the new camera. You've got the phone?
I had it. I definitely had it a second ago. It's very thin. Hold on. It's in my pocket. It's in one of my pockets.
Okay, while Theo looks for the phone, let's talk about Cinematic Squint. Pulp Phone One can now see the way you see when you forget your glasses.
Found it! It was in my hand. It was in my hand the whole time. Okay. Squint mode. Look at that. Is that a building? Nobody knows. That's cinema.
And with the new Golden Hour mode, every photo is taken at golden hour. Even at night. Even indoors. Even in a parking garage.
Our testers loved it. A few of them got sunburned. From a photo. Which we're looking into.
Hey. Marco. Wearables. Great view up here, right? We do our best thinking on the roof. We do our worst thinking in the elevator.
For years, our watch has reminded you to stand up. And for years, you've ignored it. Respectfully. We hear you.
So with Rind Watch Series Zero, we asked: what if the watch stood up for you?
That's right. Rind Watch now has legs. Four of them. Fully articulated. Fully motivated.
If you sit for more than an hour, your watch will stand up. If you sit for two hours, it will leave.
It will go for a walk without you. It will close its own rings. It will meet other watches. Some of them will come back.
We call this feature Independence. In beta testing, eighty percent of watches came home by dinner.
Rind Watch Series Zero.
An all-new leg architecture. Each leg is machined from a single piece of aluminum, and has a single piece of ambition.
Advanced health sensors measure your heart rate, your sleep, and how disappointed your watch is in you.
Marco, can I jump in? Because Rind Watch isn't just about moving. It's about understanding yourself.
With the new Sleep Score, your watch now scores your dreams. Out of ten. Most people are getting a six. We think you can do better.
And with Mood Sensing, it can tell when you're sad. And when you're sad, it plays a sad song. To match. So you're not sad alone.
We also added Emergency Small Talk via satellite. If you're ever stuck in an awkward silence, anywhere on Earth, your watch will connect to a satellite and ask about the weather.
It works in the desert. It works on a mountain. It works at your in-laws. Especially there.
Hi, I'm Priya. I lead Health. And today, I want to talk about something we all need more of. Silence.
Listen. Hear that? Birds. Wind. Someone, somewhere, explaining a podcast. Noise is everywhere.
Our earbuds already cancel noise. But noise was never the real problem. The real problem was other people.
So we're introducing Seeds Pro, with Active Conversation Cancellation. It listens to what people are saying. And then, gently, it removes them.
Your manager asks for a quick sync? Cancelled. Your neighbor wants to tell you about his boat? Cancelled. Your mother calls? Oh. Actually that one goes through. We're not monsters.
There's also an all-new Transparency mode. Tap twice, and the earbuds become fully transparent. Which is beautiful. And we strongly recommend you don't do it outdoors.
Because then you will never find them again. We've lost about four hundred in this park. If you see one, no you don't.
Seeds Pro.
Up to six hours of listening. Up to nine hours of ignoring.
Each bud contains a custom chip, a tiny speaker, and a firm belief that you deserve peace.

beats.sub: Feel more. Talk to no one.

beats.say: Of course, great hardware needs great software. So let's talk about Pulp OS One. The most personal, most private, most pulpy software we've ever made.
First, notifications. We know you get too many. So in Pulp OS One, notifications now arrive already dismissed. You'll never see them. You'll just feel them. Somewhere around your shoulders.
Next, Focus modes. In addition to Work, Sleep and Driving, we're adding a new mode called Do Not Exist. Your phone tells everyone you've moved to a farm. Very peaceful.
Autocorrect is smarter than ever. It no longer corrects what you typed. It corrects what you meant. Some of you won't like this. Autocorrect knows.
And finally, Pulp Wallet. It holds your cards, your keys, your tickets, and now your opinions. Tap to pay. Double tap to disagree.
Pulp OS One is a free update. It's available today, for every device that's thin enough to run it.
Next, the laptop. Theo, would you like to tell them what we did?
Yes. Hi again. Um. So, our laptop was already very light. And people kept asking us to make it lighter.
And we had a meeting, and someone said, what if it was lighter than air? And I laughed. And no one else laughed. So now it's lighter than air.
We replaced everything inside with a precisely engineered pocket of helium. It's the most beautiful nothing we've ever designed.
It does float. So you have to hold on to it. At all times. We lost three prototypes through the skylight. One of them is still sending us emails.
We call it PulpBook Air Air. Because it's an Air. And also, it's air.
PulpBook Air Air.
Weighing just minus two hundred grams, it's the first laptop you can lose upward.
Inside, a thirty-hour battery, a custom chip, and enough helium to make your keynote voice really funny.
And a reinforced tether port, so your work stays where you left it. Roughly.

beats.sub: Literally. Please hold on to it.

beats.say: Every great product deserves great accessories. And this year, we've thought carefully about what to protect your phone with.
This is the new Pulp Case. It's made of a soft, sustainable rubber. It's also eleven times thicker than the phone. Which is, honestly, the most protected a phone has ever been.
It even has a handle. Because at a certain point, it stopped being a case. It became luggage. And we leaned in.
And this is the Pulp Power Brick. It charges everything we make. It is, of course, not included.
In fact, it's so not included that it doesn't include itself. When you buy the brick, you receive a beautifully designed card, telling you where the brick could have been.
Pulp Case. Drop tested from space. The phone was not found.
Pulp Power Brick. Two hundred and forty watts of not being in the box.
Oh. I'm back. Okay. They told me I'd be back. I didn't believe them.
So for the home, we wanted to make something friendly. Something that listens. Something that's always on your side.
This is Pip. Pip is a home assistant. Pip has three legs and one opinion, which is yours.
You can ask Pip anything. Pip, should I have pizza for dinner again? Pip says yes. Pip, should I quit my job and become a sailor? Pip says yes.
Pip, is this a good idea? Pip says yes. Pip always says yes. We tried to make Pip say no once. Pip agreed it should say no. And then said yes.
Pip will also follow you from room to room, quietly agreeing. Our testers said it was the most supported they had ever felt.
Some of them also said it was the most followed they had ever felt. Pip agreed with them too.
Pip.
Advanced listening. Gentle nodding. Unconditional agreement.
In four colors that all agree with each other.
Every product today does something incredible. And that got us thinking.
What if a product did nothing? What if it did nothing so well that nothing else came close?
Our team spent five years on this question. Some of them are still thinking about it. We check on them every Friday.
This is Passionfruit Pebble. It has no screen. No buttons. No ports. No battery. No app.
You hold it. That's it. That's the product. And when you hold it, you'll feel something you haven't felt in years. You'll feel like you aren't being notified.
Passionfruit Pebble.
Sculpted from a single piece of ceramic, then left alone.
Never needs charging. Never needs updating. Never needs you. But it's happy you're here.
Inside, there's nothing. We checked. Twice.
Of course, none of this matters if we don't take care of the planet.
This year, all of our packaging is plastic free. Paper free. And, after a lot of hard work, box free.
Pulp Phone One now ships in nothing. It just arrives. You open the door, and it's there. Thin. Waiting.
We've also removed the cable from the box. And since there is no box, we've removed the box from the box.
By twenty thirty, we plan to be completely carbon neutral. By twenty thirty-one, we plan to be completely neutral. About everything.
So that's Pulp Phone One. Pulp Phone One Max. Rind Watch Series Zero. Seeds Pro. PulpBook Air Air. Pip. And Pebble.
It's an incredible lineup. We are so proud of our teams. And we think you're going to love them. The products. Not the teams. The teams are busy.
But before we go.
There is one more thing.
For years, people have asked us why our company is named after a fruit. And we never had a good answer.
Today, we finally do. This is the first ever Passionfruit Passionfruit.
Grown, not made. Organic, not engineered. With a triple camera system. We don't know how that happened. It was there when we picked it.
Inside, an all-new architecture of seeds and pulp, arranged with a precision that our design team describes as, quote, rude.
Pre-orders open today. Pulp Phone One ships next week. The fruit ships when it's ripe.
Can I just say, I'm really proud of this. Also, if anyone has seen a small, very thin phone, please call us. Not on that phone.
Thank you for spending this time with us. We hope it felt like holding something precious. Something light.
From all of us here at Passionfruit Park. Thank you. Have a juicy day.
